I have been farming here in Quzhou for fifty years now. My wife and I, we manage these 6 mu ourselves, though my son sends money from the city. Stevia is what I have settled on these past years — the leaf buyer comes from the processing plant and the price has been steady enough. Let me think through this season properly.

Stevia is not like wheat or maize. It is a leaf crop, and what the buyer pays for is the stevioside in the leaf, so I cannot just dump nitrogen on it like I would for grain. Too much nitrogen and the leaves grow fat but the sweetness drops — the factory tests it and docks my price. I learned this the hard way about eight years ago when I pushed urea too heavy.

I will transplant seedlings in late April, after the frost risk is gone. I buy improved seedlings from the cooperative — the old local type gives lower stevioside, maybe 8%, while the improved variety can reach 12-13%. The extra cost per mu is worth it because the buyer pays by quality grade.

For fertilizer, I base-apply compound fertilizer before transplanting — about 50 kg of 15-15-15 per mu, plus 2 bags of decomposed chicken manure my neighbor sells me. That gives me roughly 7-8 kg N, 7-8 kg P2O5, 7-8 kg K2O from the compound. Then I top-dress twice: once after the plants establish (around 15 days), and once after the first cutting. Total N around 14 kg/mu — any more and quality suffers. Potassium I push a bit higher because K helps the sweet compound, so I add extra potassium sulfate, bringing K2O to about 16 kg. Phosphorus around 9 kg is enough since stevia does not need much.

Well water here is reliable. Stevia roots are shallow so it dries out fast — I irrigate about 6 times through the season, more after each cutting to push regrowth. I take two cuttings, sometimes three if the weather holds.

Pests: aphids and leafhoppers are the main worry, and sometimes leaf spot in humid weeks. I spray about 4 times — two preventive, two when I see damage. I rotary till before transplanting; no need for deep ploughing on this crop.

Expected dried leaf yield: I have been getting around 280 kg/mu the last three years. I will aim for 300 this year.
